A Zürich restaurant serving Malaysian, Chinese, and Taiwanese home favourites.
clients.description: MenuDash — 959 visits in its first 18 days, more than the restaurant's homepage. After the third PDF menu they asked for, I proposed an online menu instead, and they paid for it: three table QR codes became one, opening a menu guests filter by language and diet. A wrong spreadsheet gets a report and a rollback, never a broken page.

clients.linkInfo: My own product: a spreadsheet in, a print-ready menu out.
clients.description: CSV in, print-ready menu out, replacing layout work I redid by hand on every price change. Built and deployed solo in four months, 130 commits: product, design, build and deploy.

clients.linkInfo: A Zürich restaurant serving Malaysian, Chinese, and Taiwanese home favourites.
clients.description: Still in use two years on, and staff update it without a designer: a multilingual menu system (EN/DE/zh-TW) with dietary tagging, handed over in Canva. The process problem it exposed became menuGen.

clients.linkInfo: A Swiss manufacturer of customizable high-quality bikes and e-bikes.
clients.description: 10K+ YouTube views, ~5× the channel average, for a SwissRider e-bike promo. I proposed the storyboard to the CMO and produced the animation.

clients.linkInfo: Fashion startup transitioning from handcrafted to digital e-commerce.
clients.description: +35% orders after taking a Taipei fashion label from Instagram DMs to a live online store: product strategy, UX, and the storefront and checkout, set up on a commerce platform.

experience.title: Research Intern (Frontend & AI Engineering)
experience.linkInfo: A lab advancing visual computing, AI, and filmmaking technologies.
experience.role: Embedded in the animation team, reporting to the engineers who turn the lab's research code into production tools. I owned a script-visualisation platform end to end, which Walt Disney Studios stakeholders piloted, and built an AI pipeline prototype over ~100 confidential recordings in which every answer traces back to its timestamped source. My three-month contract was extended by another three.

experience.title: XR Software Engineer Intern
experience.linkInfo: A Swiss startup specializing in motion tracking for VR/AR.
experience.role: Self-directed at a six-person motion-tracking startup: I shipped three XR interaction prototypes in the run-up to the company's CES 2025 showing, and the CTO reviewed each one. One was the interaction layer for the Maliang Magic Pencil, where the version I worked on had a single button to carry painting, selection and manipulation. Behind it is a state manager that keeps interaction logic independent of the hardware. I also found and fixed a component-lifecycle defect in a third-party XR framework's source.

experience.title: Research and Teaching Assistant
experience.company: Dept. Architecture of Tamkang University - CCC Lab
experience.role: CCC Lab, under Prof. Chen-Cheng Chen. I took over a VIVE tracking rig, integrated it into the lab's robotic fabrication system, and built a double-curved wall inside a building under construction: 1,430 bricks across 52 layers, every one laid by a UR10 robot arm, from 22 base positions the model chose for reach and sequencing. I also assisted on programming and parametric-modelling courses for ~60 architecture students, explaining code to people who had never written any.
